scope: Five toolchain-qualification pytest cases, not application workflow implementation, original AT acceptance, or production Temporal. H0 separately authorized the preserved isolated installation.

owners.main: scripts/ifpmic_temporal_toolchain.py launch/verification/owned-stop helper and scripts/verify_ifpmic_b03_h1.py runner; integration and source/evidence protection.
owners.tc: tests/ifpmic_api/test_temporal_toolchain.py and temporal_toolchain_fixture.py; independent sentinel, fixed fixture workflow, SDK client and worker subprocesses, history/retention/duplicate assertions.

guard_interface.verify_binary: verify_binary(path, expected_sha256): absolute nonsymlink regular file; compare SHA before ELF checks; require >=64 bytes, ELF magic/class64/little-endian and x86_64 machine62; fixed HASH_MISMATCH or ARTIFACT_INVALID codes; never PATH lookup/download. Approved actual hash comes from the frozen runner, not HTTP/CLI caller input.
guard_interface.start_server: start_server(binary, expected_sha256, data_dir, ports, *, log_name): verify_binary before creating data dir/files or spawning; validate exactly three distinct loopback ports1..65535, safe basename log_name; private0700 directory, log0600, literal empty JSON {} env file0600; fixed argv and sanitized env; Popen start_new_session=True with recorded PID/startticks. Same owned data_dir/store reused on second launch; unique log per launch; no deletion of unknown data.
guard_interface.stop_owned: stop_owned(Popen): poll same handle and confirm saved PID/startticks before signalling; SIGTERM then wait10s, if still same owned live identity SIGKILL and wait5s. Reap original handle; no name/port-only killing; record forced cleanup and fail positive integration if clean shutdown deadline was exceeded. No source changes or reruns during live gate.
guard_interface.stop_all_owned: stop_all_owned(handles,total_timeout): fence each saved PID/starttick, SIGTERM all live handles before any wait, bounded shared wait up to10s, then SIGKILL same still-live identities and reap under one absolute deadline. Return per-handle stopped/forced status; do not rediscover ownership by process name/port. Used by TC finally and runner failure cleanup.

negative_cases.wrong_hash: Harmless sentinel script with wrong expected64hex digest; require HASH_MISMATCH, sentinel not invoked, no data directory created.
negative_cases.missing: Absent path with fixed expected digest; ARTIFACT_INVALID before process/files.
negative_cases.truncated: 8-byte ELF prefix with its matching expected SHA; ARTIFACT_INVALID due incomplete ELF, no process/files. These test the same main helper used by positive server launch.

server_launch.environment: Only PATH plus explicitly required no-bytecode/test settings; no ambient TEMPORAL/proxy/cloud/auth/PG variables. Do not repurpose HOME. Env-file literal {} is private, not an ambient user file. No WorkflowEnvironment/server-download helpers.
server_launch.network: Allocate three distinct loopback ports; inspect actual owned listeners (/proc/socket or equivalent) and fail non-loopback server sockets; headless prevents UI/news activity. SDK clients target only explicit127.0.0.1:frontend.
server_launch.readiness: Separate SDK client process Client.connect then workflow_service.describe_namespace(DescribeNamespaceRequest(namespace="default"), rpc_timeout=timedelta(seconds=5)); retry only RPC UNAVAILABLE/DEADLINE_EXCEEDED or connection startup errors under30s/100ms cadence; other errors fail immediately.
server_launch.retention: Read namespace response.config.workflow_execution_retention_ttl seconds+nanos/1e9 and assert >3600 before workflow start; record actual value before/after restart. This reads config, does not prove expiry behavior.
server_launch.prestart_loopback_basis: Pinned official CLI v1.9.1 source observation verifies FrontendIP flows to frontend/internal RPC BindOnIP, frontend HTTP config and metrics listen address. Actual owned socket inspection still required; source observation is not reproducible binary attestation.

fixture_protocol.workflow: TC-only deterministic class IFPMICH1SyntheticWait. run(marker) stores fixed h1-synthetic-v1 marker, awaits finish signal via workflow.wait_condition, returns fixed h1-finished-v1. query phase returns waiting/finished; signal finish sets flag. No business steps, artifacts or quality PASS.
fixture_protocol.entrypoint: Pinned new venv/bin/python tests/ifpmic_api/temporal_toolchain_fixture.py with subcommands worker/probe; subprocess CLI carries only owned endpoint, queue/workflow IDs and evidence paths, no secrets. Ensure repo root/module importability without extra packages. Worker uses SDK default sandbox.
fixture_protocol.phase1: Create worker process1 and separate client/probe process1. Query confirms wait; namespace retention>3600; start exactly one unique synthetic ID with WorkflowIDReusePolicy.REJECT_DUPLICATE and WorkflowIDConflictPolicy.FAIL. Duplicate while running must raise temporalio.exceptions.WorkflowAlreadyStartedError with original run_id. Capture private full history JSON and normalized ordered event_id/event_type list after wait/duplicate check; no second logical run. Client1 exits0 then stop/reap worker1 and server1, proving their saved process identities absent.
fixture_protocol.phase2: Start server2 using same binary/store/ports; new worker2 and client2. Existing exact ID yields same original run_id, and every recorded phase1 event_id/type remains an identical ordered prefix. Query still waiting; signal finish once; result equals h1-finished-v1. Duplicate closed ID with same reject policies must raise same typed error and preserve original result/run_id; no second run (actual list/describe). Retention remains >3600. Client2 exits0; worker2/server2 stop/reap.
fixture_protocol.history: Actual SDK fetch_history()/WorkflowHistory.to_json(); ordered event IDs strict increasing, first WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_STARTED, before restart no WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_COMPLETED, after signal final WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_COMPLETED and literal fixture result. Preserve raw histories private; public event-type/count/hash summaries only.
fixture_protocol.typed_errors: SDK1.34 _impl.py maps ALREADY_EXISTS with WorkflowExecutionAlreadyStartedFailure detail to WorkflowAlreadyStartedError. Both running and closed tests require exact type and matching run_id; generic exception assertions forbidden.
fixture_protocol.processes: Two distinct actual CLI processes, two distinct actual worker processes, two distinct client/probe processes; record PID/startticks privately and verify old identities absent before reuse of ports/store. pytest is a separate parent. Worker termination may be graceful SDK shutdown handler; no reuse of worker/client objects across server restart.

deadlines.integration_exception_justification: One case includes two actual server/worker/client lifecycles, persistent store recovery, retention/history/RPC polling and exact owned cleanup. A reviewed240s exception is within the unchanged300s Python phase; this is not a threshold waiver after execution.

Enforce source fingerprints before execution.
gate.after: Exactly5 passed/0failed/0errors/0skips, each normal<=30s and integration<=240s; fresh JUnit IDs match independent inventory; source/config/lock and old environment unchanged, package/binary pins unchanged; all owned process identities gone and listeners released. Failures preserve candidate/raw logs/history and execute exact-handle cleanup; never restart on observation timeout.

deadline_enforcement.mechanism: TC autouse pytest fixture in main thread uses signal.setitimer(signal.ITIMER_REAL) plus monotonic absolute deadlines. Ordinary case body budget25s with5s reserved cleanup; integration body215s with25s reserved cleanup. Case total includes fixture teardown and must remain<=30/240s in JUnit. Handler raises a fixed CaseDeadlineExceeded failure, never xfail/skip. Save/restore previous handler/timer.
deadline_enforcement.propagation: Every subprocess.run/wait, readiness loop, RPC and worker-query wait uses min(contract sublimit, remaining monotonic body budget); zero remaining raises immediately. Child probe/worker handlers also have fixed internal deadlines; client RPC5s and process phase30s never extend parent case budget. Tests cannot catch the timeout and continue business probes.
deadline_enforcement.on_timeout: Enter unconditional finally cleanup with a fresh absolute cleanup deadline within reserved5/25s. First SIGTERM all still-owned handles concurrently after PID/starttick verification, wait at most10s total (or remaining budget for ordinary case), then SIGKILL still-same owned identities and reap within remaining cleanup budget. No serial10s per child accumulation. Retain failure and raw records. Forced cleanup fails positive case.
deadline_enforcement.cleanup_watchdog: Arm a separate ITIMER_REAL timer for the reserved cleanup window while cleanup runs; expiration fails case and leaves complete private owned-process ledger for outer runner cleanup. Normal cleanup also consumes the reserved budget and observed total remains checked. Restore timers after cleanup; never reset the primary body deadline per operation.
deadline_enforcement.outer_watchdog: Runner independently enforces overall pytest300s. On timeout, snapshot current proven pytest descendants (PPID ancestry +startticks) and recorded owned process identities before signalling/reaping pytest, then fence/terminate/kill/reap only these owned identities. Preserve exact PID/starttick ledger privately. This is cleanup after a failed gate, never acceptance or permission to restart.
deadline_enforcement.evidence: JUnit per-case elapsed, body/cleanup start/end and timeout outcome in private ledger; public durations/counts only. Reviewer checks actual implementation before first run.
